summary.text: CA9 has the strongest convergent evidence in this analysis. It leads the overall convergence ranking and sits near the top of both question-specific profiles, because every independent layer points the same way: the RNA increase in CPTAC replicates in TCGA-KIRC [gene=CA9; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=9.71], it survives extrapolation to a pure tumour [gene=CA9; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=7.787], tumour cells make nearly all of its transcripts in two single-cell datasets, and clinical antibodies (girentuximab) and imaging agents already exist. Its weaknesses are just as clear: it is not a dependency of ccRCC cells, it stains the normal stomach, and it varies across tumour cells. It is therefore best used as a homing antigen for imaging, radioligands or conjugates, not as a gene to switch off.

A second tier of tumour-cell targets is supported by data, literature and drugs together. CD70 is increased at RNA and protein level, replicates in TCGA and already has clinical antibodies, although one single-cell dataset attributes part of it to T cells. NNMT is tumour-intrinsic in both single-cell datasets, its protein increase replicates strongly in the confirmatory CPTAC cohort [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=4.776], and the literature describes it as a prognostic biomarker with selective inhibitors. SCARB1 tops the data-only target profile and replicates in the confirmatory cohort, but it is shared with endothelium and macrophages and is enriched in the normal adrenal gland. SLC16A3 (MCT4) replicates at protein level and is linked in the literature to lactate-driven immune evasion. ENPP3 is a validated conjugate target whose strong staining in normal kidney narrows its window. HK2, in contrast, does not replicate in the confirmatory cohort and loses weight.

The best biomarkers are mostly genes that tumours lose. PSAT1, PCK1 and ALDH6A1 lead the biomarker profile: each is decreased in tumours, the decrease replicates in TCGA, and each is prognostic, with ALDH6A1 the strongest favourable marker [gene=ALDH6A1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=-0.554]. The PSAT1 protein decrease also replicates in the confirmatory cohort. Several leaders of the overall ranking, such as ALDOB and UMOD, belong to the same pattern of lost proximal-tubule identity, whereas COXFA4L2 (NDUFA4L2) is a hypoxia-driven gene that rises with CA9. These genes describe the disease and its prognosis; they are rarely targets.

Unexplored candidates. Because the convergence ranking rewards literature and existing drugs, little-studied genes can only surface through the discovery screen, and two tumour-track genes stand out there; they are identified and prioritised for experimental validation, not discovered or proven. COL23A1, a transmembrane collagen, is made by tumour cells, its increase replicates in TCGA and survives extrapolation to a pure tumour [gene=COL23A1; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88], its protein is increased, and it is antibody-tractable with no clinical drug. What is missing is proof that the protein is reachable at the cell surface (the CSPA surfaceome did not observe it), normal-tissue staining, any dependency, and homogeneity: in the weakest quarter of donors few tumour cells express it. Immunohistochemistry on tumour and normal tissue arrays, followed by surface-binding and internalisation assays with an antibody, would test it. RAB42, a small GTPase, is also tumour-cell derived, replicated in TCGA and purity-robust, but its location is not established and no selective dependency is seen, so knockdown in ccRCC models and localisation studies come first. In this literature corpus neither gene has a sentence, although the screen counts a handful of ccRCC papers by symbol, so the analysis may reinforce earlier observations rather than open a new field. The strongest stromal candidate, OLFML2A, is a secreted fibroblast protein, and the leading immune-track genes (MILR1, LILRB4) vanish at purity one, so they mark infiltration rather than tumour cells.

Several established drug targets are microenvironment or mechanism genes rather than tumour-cell targets. KDR (VEGFR2), the target of approved angiogenesis inhibitors, is made by endothelium, and EPAS1 (HIF-2 alpha, target of belzutifan) is expressed by endothelium and fibroblasts as well as tumour cells, so bulk omics understate it. The disease mechanism is anchored by recurrent VHL, PBRM1, SETD2 and BAP1 mutations and by loss of the chromosome arm that carries VHL and PBRM1, and RPS6KB1, downstream of mTOR, is the most activated kinase. No candidate is a selective DepMap dependency, and trial associations do not separate treatment arms, so every call here is a prioritisation, not proof of benefit.

omics.text: In CPTAC tumour-versus-normal data the strongest increased products with protein confirmation are CA9 [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.27], COXFA4L2 [gene=COXFA4L2; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=3.77], NNMT [gene=NNMT; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.71], CD70 and SLC16A3, all hypoxia or metabolic genes downstream of VHL loss. The strongest decreased products, such as ALDOB [gene=ALDOB; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=-2.27] and UMOD [gene=UMOD; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=-2.24], reflect the loss of normal tubule identity and serve as tissue biomarkers.

EPAS1 shows why bulk omics can mislead for a validated target: its protein is increased [gene=EPAS1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=1.16] while the RNA change is small [gene=EPAS1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=0.306], and endothelial cells also express it. HIF-2 alpha is regulated post-translationally, so it would never top an expression-based ranking despite being the target of an approved drug.

literature.text: The literature corpus supports the leading targets directly. CA9 is described as preferentially enriched in ccRCC tumour cells and as a PET imaging target (PMID 42473996); CD70 as commonly overexpressed in renal cell carcinoma with minimal normal-tissue expression (PMID 38195301) and as the basis of new radiotracers (PMID 39510586); NNMT as a prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target with worse survival at high expression (PMID 41399267). SLC16A3 is linked to lactate-driven immune evasion through M2 macrophages (PMID 42028950).

The literature is silent where the data are strong. SCARB1, the top gene of the data-only target profile, and the discovery candidates COL23A1 and RAB42 have no extracted relation or sentence in this corpus, and FCER1G, which the literature proposes as a prognostic marker, turns out to be an infiltration signal in the purity analysis.

external.text: Open Targets separates established from untested targets. VHL has the top association with ccRCC and EPAS1 a strong one, with belzutifan approved against HIF-2 alpha; KDR is hit by many approved kinase inhibitors such as axitinib, cabozantinib and pazopanib; CA9 has girentuximab in late clinical development, CD70 has cusatuzumab and vorsetuzumab mafodotin, and ENPP3 had the conjugate AGS-16C3F. SCARB1 is a membrane protein with genetic association but no clinical drug, and NNMT and SLC16A3 are tractable but undrugged in the clinic.

Druggability without dependency is a weaker target case, and that applies to almost every candidate here. CA9 has no CRISPR effect in ccRCC lines [gene=CA9; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; mean_effect_ccrcc=0.051]; SCD has an effect that is not selective; EPAS1 shows the most selective dependency but does not pass correction; and the hexokinase inhibitor tested against HK2 does not kill ccRCC lines selectively.

cells.text: Single-cell data decide which bulk candidates are tumour-intrinsic. CA9 [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=97.6%] and NNMT are made almost entirely by tumour cells, and both calls replicate in the Zhang 2021 dataset. SCARB1 is not tumour-specific: tumour cells hold only part of its transcripts [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=33.6%], with endothelium expressing it most per cell. CD70 changes call between datasets because T cells also express it.

Several known drug targets are microenvironment genes, not tumour-cell targets. KDR is endothelial [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=95.1%], CD74 is made by myeloid and dendritic cells, and CXCR4 by infiltrating lymphocytes, so drugs against them act on the vessels or the immune infiltrate.

spatial.text: In Visium sections the spatial picture matches the single-cell attribution. High-CA9 spots are explained by tumour cells [gene=CA9; type=spatial_expresser; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; cell_group=RCC; composition_corrected_share=0.999] and sit among other tumour cells, while high-KDR spots are explained by endothelium [gene=KDR; type=spatial_expresser; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; cell_group=Endothelial; composition_corrected_share=0.99] and their neighbours are enriched for endothelial cells, with tumour cells close by.

structure.text: Structural-context scores are descriptive heuristics computed on predicted AlphaFold monomers; they are not evidence of a degron, ligase compatibility or degradation, and no curated experimental degron or ternary-complex reference was used for these candidates. CA9 has a moderately confident model with cavities that recover part of its known ligand-contact residues [gene=CA9; type=ligand_site_validation; source=PDBe-KB ligand sites (experimental holo structures); recall=0.5]. KDR has one of the highest descriptive scores [gene=KDR; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; structural_context_score=0.841], and COL23A1 has a low-confidence model [gene=COL23A1; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=58.91] with no reliable cavity, which favours antibody approaches for it.

discovery.text: COL23A1 is a transmembrane collagen and the leading tumour-track candidate of the discovery screen, which looks for genes increased in both CPTAC RNA and protein, attributed to one cell type, little studied in ccRCC and without a clinical drug. Tumour cells make most of its tumour transcripts [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881]. The increase replicates in TCGA-KIRC [gene=COL23A1; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=5.829] and survives extrapolation to a pure tumour, so it is not infiltration. It is not prognostic and no ccRCC line depends on it. Its conjugate suitability is high, but staining data are missing, the surfaceome did not observe it, and only a small share of tumour cells express it in the weakest donors [gene=COL23A1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=7.5].

RAB42 is a small GTPase, the second tumour-track candidate. Tumour cells make most of its transcripts [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627]. The increase replicates in TCGA-KIRC [gene=RAB42; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=4.371] and is purity-robust [gene=RAB42; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=3.189]. Its surface location is not established, so antibody access is uncertain; it is not prognostic, and no selective dependency is seen, so it needs functional knockdown work before it can be called a target.

The stroma and immune tracks must be read separately. In the stroma track, OLFML2A is a secreted fibroblast protein whose increase replicates in TCGA and survives at purity one, while COX4I2 is an internal mitochondrial subunit that antibodies cannot reach. The immune track, which holds most of the pool, is dominated by macrophage genes: MILR1 and LILRB4 replicate in TCGA, but their bulk increase nearly vanishes at purity one [gene=MILR1; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.414], so they are infiltration-driven markers of hot tumours. All discovery genes are data-ranked hypotheses; none is a selective dependency.

validation.text: External replication strengthens most leaders. The increases of CA9, CD70, SCARB1, ENPP3 and the decreases of PSAT1 and PCK1 all replicate in TCGA-KIRC paired samples, and NNMT and PSAT1 are prognostic there. In the confirmatory CPTAC cohort, with different patients and technology, the protein calls of NNMT, SCARB1, SLC16A3 and PSAT1 replicate, whereas HK2 does not [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-0.256]; CA9 was too sparse to test there, which is not a failure to replicate.

Driver status, dependency, kinase activity and purity sort the rest. Only VHL, PBRM1, SETD2 and BAP1 are recurrent drivers, and PBRM1 loss lowers its own RNA and protein, a real dosage effect. No candidate target is a selective dependency in DepMap. After protein adjustment, RPS6KB1 is the most activated kinase [gene=RPS6KB1; type=kinase_activity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PHOSPHOSITE; ksea_z=3.289], in line with mTOR pathway activity. The purity check weakens FCER1G, MILR1 and LILRB4, whose changes shrink in a pure tumour, and strengthens CA9, CD70, SCARB1 and COL23A1, whose changes persist.

robustness.text: Under random re-weighting of the evidence streams, a few positions are stable. In the target profile SCARB1, CA9, SLC16A3, CD70 and NNMT stay in the top ten in the large majority of draws with narrow rank intervals, and in the biomarker profile PSAT1 is the most stable leader, followed by PCK1 and SLC6A19. In the overall convergence ranking only CA9 and COXFA4L2 are robust top-ten genes.

Other positions depend on the chosen weights. Lower in the target profile (for example PNCK, TNFAIP6 and SCD) the chance of staying in the top ten collapses although the top-twenty-five position holds, and several biomarker leaders such as CA9, FCER1G and PROM2 have wide rank intervals because their score rests on one or two streams. These candidates should be treated as weight-dependent.

treatment.text: In IMmotion150, no gene separates atezolizumab plus bevacizumab from sunitinib after correction, so trial results are associations only. Higher CD70 is associated with longer benefit on the combination [gene=CD70; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab_bevacizumab.log_hr_per_sd=-0.383], with an adjusted p-value of [gene=CD70; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab_bevacizumab.padj=0.166], and higher CA9 with longer benefit on sunitinib, again without significance. In the CheckMate trial of nivolumab versus everolimus, NNMT shows no association with outcome. None of these are predictive markers.

subtypes.text: CA9 is the clearest subgroup candidate: it is higher in PBRM1-mutant tumours in TCGA [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.148] and is flagged as a PBRM1 subgroup target, consistent with the literature linking CA9-targeted PET uptake to PBRM1 loss, and it is higher in ccA than ccB tumours. PSAT1 behaves the other way, higher in ccB and BAP1-mutant tumours [gene=PSAT1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; BAP1.tcga_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=1.711], in line with aggressive disease. CD70 does not change consistently with any driver. Immune genes can differ between subgroups only because of infiltration.

adc.text: For antibody-drug conjugates or radioligands, CD70 ranks near the top of the suitability screen [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.746] with no vital-organ protein enrichment, though staining data are missing. The known controls behave as expected but show the limits: CA9 stains the stomach and is heterogeneous across tumour cells, and ENPP3 stains normal kidney strongly. The discovery gene COL23A1 scores high [gene=COL23A1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.705], but without staining data, surfaceome confirmation or homogeneous expression a high score does not show a conjugate would work.

immune.text: Immune-cell genes mark hot tumours rather than tumour cells. The checkpoint control PDCD1 is almost entirely immune-made and tracks CD8 T cells, and CD74 and LILRB4 behave similarly; LILRB4 follows the overall immune score closely [gene=LILRB4; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; rho_with_immune_score=0.853]. These are microenvironment targets whose bulk signal depends on infiltration, which is why they vanish in a pure tumour, whereas SLC16A3 is a tumour-cell gene that the literature links to immune suppression.

integration.text: Omics, literature and external knowledge converge on the hypoxia programme switched on by VHL loss: CA9, CD70, NNMT and SLC16A3 are increased, tumour-intrinsic, replicated and described in the literature, and CA9 and CD70 already have clinical agents. They disagree on SCARB1, which is strongly supported by data but silent in the literature and shared with stroma, and on FCER1G, which is supported by literature but driven by infiltration. EPAS1 and KDR are validated drug targets that expression data rank low, because HIF-2 alpha is regulated as a protein and KDR lives in the vessels.

By role, CA9, CD70, ENPP3 and SCARB1 are surface targets best approached with antibodies, conjugates or radioligands; NNMT and SLC16A3 are enzymatic or transporter targets for small molecules that also have biomarker value; PSAT1, PCK1, ALDH6A1 and VWF are biomarkers; VHL, PBRM1, SETD2, BAP1 and RPS6KB1 explain the mechanism; and COL23A1 and RAB42 are exploratory first-in-class hypotheses.

targets.rationale: Top of the overall ranking and near the top of both profiles: tumour-intrinsic in two single-cell datasets, replicated in TCGA, robust to re-weighting, with clinical antibodies and PET imaging. Best used as a homing antigen, since it is not a dependency and stains the stomach.

Increased at RNA and protein level, replicated in TCGA, purity-robust, top-ranked for conjugate suitability and already targeted by clinical antibodies; the cell attribution partly includes T cells and staining data are missing.

Tumour-intrinsic in both single-cell datasets, protein increase replicated strongly in the confirmatory cohort, prognostic in TCGA and supported by literature with selective inhibitors; ranked above SCARB1 here because its cell source is cleaner.

First in the data-only target profile and replicated in TCGA and the confirmatory cohort, but placed below CA9, CD70 and NNMT because endothelium and macrophages share its expression, the adrenal gland is enriched for it and no drug exists.
Robust in the target profile, protein and phosphosite replicated in the confirmatory cohort, and linked in the literature to lactate-driven immune evasion; no clinical drug and no dependency.

Validated by the approved drug belzutifan and the most selective dependency checked, though not significant; ranked low by expression because HIF-2 alpha is regulated as a protein and is also expressed by stroma.
Increased and replicated, surface-confirmed in the surfaceome and a known conjugate target, but strong staining in normal kidney and duodenum narrows its window.
Leader and most stable gene of the biomarker profile: decreased in tumours, replicated in TCGA and the confirmatory cohort, prognostic, and higher in ccB and BAP1-mutant tumours.
Lost in tumours with a real copy-number dosage effect and the strongest favourable prognostic association among the biomarker leaders.
Lost in tumours at protein level, replicated in TCGA and favourable when retained: a robust marker of lost tubule identity.

Exploratory: leading tumour-track discovery candidate, tumour-cell derived, replicated in TCGA and purity-robust, antibody-tractable with no drug; the main limitation is that surface accessibility, normal-tissue staining, homogeneity and any dependency are unproven.

Exploratory: second tumour-track discovery candidate, tumour-cell derived, replicated in TCGA and purity-robust; the main limitation is that its location is not established and no dependency or function in ccRCC has been shown.

limitations.text: Associations in CPTAC, TCGA and the trials are not causal, and no candidate was tested functionally in this analysis.
No leading target is a selective DepMap dependency, and two-dimensional cell lines miss HIF-2 biology, so dependency evidence is weak across the board.
Trial associations come from single arms of modest size and no gene separates treatment arms after correction; they are leads, not predictive markers.
Structural-context scores describe predicted monomers and are not evidence of degrons, ligase compatibility or degradation.
The literature corpus covers a few hundred ccRCC abstracts; absence of a sentence here does not mean absence in PubMed, and discovery novelty is counted by gene symbol.
Staining data are missing for several conjugate candidates (CD70, COL23A1), and CA9 could not be tested in the confirmatory protein cohort.

This single-agent run covered fewer genes per layer than five specialists would; some candidates (for example SLC6A19, CYP2J2, FABP6, ANGPTL4) were not profiled in every layer. The overall convergence_ranking tool call timed out and the overall ranking was read from convergence.json.
Passing the automatic checks means no failures were detected by them; it is not complete scientific validation.
